title: Veterans Pension One-Time Declarations — Weight by Date of Deposit
content:
# Weighing a one-time declaration by deposit date — Veterans Pension

What counts in a Veterans Pension one-time payment declaration is weighed by when the most recent retroactive Disability Compensation release was deposited — its payment date in the compensation payment ledger — counted in days to the declaration — the day the veteran files it, not the date the declaration carries:

| Most recent release deposited | Weight |
|---|---|
| within the fresh period: 90 days or fewer before the declaration | counts in full |
| more than 90 days but within one year (365 days) | the months left of its twelve-month year divided by 12 — 12 less the whole months from the deposit to the filing day, divided by 12 |
| more than 365 days before | nothing counts |

The weight is applied to the releases less any fee taken out, as far as they count by the months they were paid for, and the declared amount is rounded to the cent.

## Hypothetical figures (amount counting before weighting: 6000.00)

| Deposited | Whole months since | Declared |
|---|---|---|
| 60 days before | — | 6000.00 |
| 140 days before | 4 | 6000.00 multiplied by 8, divided by 12: 4000.00 |
| 400 days before | 13 | 0.00 |
